title: Forces and Movement
seo_title: Primary 2 Basic Science: Forces and Movement Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: Primary 2 Basic Science: You and Energy
standard_text: Forces (pushes and pulls) change the motion and shape of objects; friction slows moving objects; gravity pulls objects toward the Earth. Pupils observe, measure and predict the effects of forces. (summary of the Basic Science curriculum, Primary 2, theme: You and Energy)
meta_desc: Free Primary 2 Basic Science worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: You and Energy): pushes and pulls, friction, gravity, patterns of motion and force investigations. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A force is a push or a pull.
key_sub: Friction slows things down; gravity pulls things toward Earth.
body_html:
How to think about it

A force is a push or a pull. Forces can start, stop, speed up, slow down or turn an object.

  • Contact forces happen when objects touch, like friction and pushes.
  • Non-contact forces act from a distance, like gravity and magnetism.
  • Smooth surfaces like ice have little friction; rough surfaces like carpet have more.
Example

Which force pulls a ball down a slide?

It always pulls down.

Answer: gravity

Example

Why does a rolling ball stop on grass?

Rubbing surfaces

Answer: friction slows it down

Common mistakes

  • Thinking moving objects stop because they 'run out of force'.
  • Thinking gravity only acts on heavy objects.
  • Thinking friction is always bad.

items.q: Why does a ball roll faster down a steep ramp than a gentle one?
c: The steep ramp has more friction.
Gravity pulls it more along the steep slope.
Gravity is weaker on gentle ramps.
The ball is heavier on steep ramps.
items.e: Steeper slopes speed things up.

items.q: Is friction helpful or unhelpful here: parts rubbing inside a car engine?
items.e: Friction is useful for grip and stopping, but a problem when it slows things or wears them out.
